:::{#rem-quadratic-form-scalar}
#### Like the derivative of $cx^2$

This operation is like taking the derivative of $cx^2$ with respect to $x$ in non-vector calculus:
$\deriv{x} (cx^2) = 2cx$,
and @thm-quadratic-form says $\deriv{\vcoef} (\tp{\vcoef} \matr{S} \vcoef) = 2 \matr{S} \vcoef$.
For example, with $p = 1$, $\matr{S} = (3)$, and $\vcoef = (\coef{1})$,
$\tp{\vcoef} \matr{S} \vcoef = 3\coef{1}^2$,
and its derivative is $6\coef{1} = 2 \matr{S} \vcoef$.

:::
